clue.text: Want you coming back as a servant

parts.note: to want is to lack, be without

indicators.note: coming back tells us to read the archaic word for you from right to left

parts.note: ye is the old plural form of you

explanation.surface: Someone who lacks things returns to work as a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lackey is a footman or servile follower, a synonym for a servant.

clue.text: What may be trumpeted as the ultimate appointment

definitions.meaning: a bugle call sounded at military funerals and remembrance services
read literally, a final job or position

explanation.surface: A fanfare sounded for someone's final job.
explanation.definitionFit: The Last Post is the bugle call played at military funerals; literally it is a final post or job.

clue.text: Caring terribly about hospital's discomfiture

indicators.note: about means going around, so the anagram encloses the letter
terribly signals the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital's distress at providing appalling care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns CARING into CAGRIN; 'about' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is annoyance or embarrassment at failure, which is discomfiture.

clue.text: Old numbers I have put down as 'great'

parts.note: ex means former or old
tens are numbers
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Old figures recorded as great by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Extensive means large in extent, so great in size or scope.

clue.text: No amateur, frightfully crude TV executive?

parts.note: someone who is no amateur is a professional, a pro

indicators.note: frightfully suggests disorder, so the letters of crude are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seasoned professional in television whose output is shockingly crude.
explanation.definitionFit: A producer is an executive who oversees television programmes; the question mark admits producers work elsewhere too.

clue.text: Op is third-rate — a terrible practitioner at the hospital

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An operation done poorly by an awful hospital practitioner.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiotherapist treats patients with radiation, a specialist working in a hospital.

clue.text: Dull service — start to snore in it

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the other word

parts.note: duty is service, as in on duty

indicators.note: start to picks out the first letter of snore

explanation.surface: A boring stint of work during which one begins to snore.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty can mean dry and dull, as in a dusty, uninteresting answer.

clue.text: Cold drink please, but only half that squash!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
rum is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: only half means just the first half of the word please

explanation.surface: Ordering a cold drink, but only half a glass of squash.
explanation.definitionFit: To crumple is to crush or squash something out of shape.

clue.text: Bit of cloth left to be patched to a new garment

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A scrap of fabric patched onto a new item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A raglan is a coat with sleeves running to the collar, named after Lord Raglan.

clue.text: Ordinary components of pudding?

definitions.meaning: the main ingredients of a classic baked British dessert

explanation.surface: Asking what goes into an everyday pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means basic or routine, and the two foods make the British bread and butter pudding.

clue.text: He started badly, becoming exhausted

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone made a poor start and ended up worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattered is informal British usage for utterly tired, a synonym of exhausted.

clue.text: Hurled from front of seat on to airbag?

indicators.note: front of picks out just the opening letter of seat

parts.note: a lung is jokingly an airbag in the body

explanation.surface: A car passenger thrown forward from the seat onto the deployed airbag.
explanation.definitionFit: Slung is the past tense of sling, meaning thrown or hurled.

clue.text: Quiet country has endless fish

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
Iran is a country in the Middle East

indicators.note: endless means the word has loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A peaceful nation that has a never-ending supply of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The piranha is a sharp-toothed South American freshwater fish.

clue.text: Thinking of 'eaven, mum keeping pious and plain

parts.note: holy with its H dropped, as in the cockney 'eaven for heaven, gives 'oly

indicators.note: keeping means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, mum
pi is a short informal word for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A Cockney mother, dreaming of heaven, remains devout and unadorned.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'eaven is the hint to drop an H from HOLY, giving OLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia is a plain in the western Peloponnese, site of the ancient Olympic Games.

clue.text: Saint at home, very good place for getting orders from above

definitions.text: place for getting orders from above

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
A1 (written AI) means first-rate, very good

explanation.surface: A saint stays at home in a fine spot to receive divine instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Sinai is where Moses received the Ten Commandments, orders from God above.

clue.text: Vulnerable warrior getting a cold starts to expect sympathy

parts.note: a chill is a cold, a minor illness

indicators.note: starts to tells us to take the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A warrior who catches a cold and starts hoping for sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: Achilles was vulnerable only at his heel, where his mother held him when dipping him in the Styx.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles was the Greek hero of the Trojan War, invulnerable except at one heel.

clue.text: Weird Len, native of land to the east

indicators.note: weird signals the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd man called Len, a native of an eastern country.
explanation.definitionFit: Levantine means of the Levant, the lands of the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Like an old church lane with yews here and there

indicators.note: here and there suggests letters scattered about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old church on a lane dotted with yew trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Wesleyan describes the Methodist church founded by John Wesley in the 18th century.

clue.text: Fighter scurried — trouble, right?

parts.note: tore means rushed or scurried
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A fighter rushed off, asking whether trouble was right.
explanation.definitionFit: A toreador is a bullfighter, especially one on horseback.

clue.text: Pompous orator's beginning to get pot-bellied?

indicators.note: beginning picks out the opening letter of orator's

parts.note: rotund means round and plump, pot-bellied

explanation.surface: A self-important speaker who is starting to put on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Orotund describes speech that is pompous or bombastic in style.

clue.text: Grass edging church official cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a verger is a church official who looks after the building

explanation.surface: A church officer trims the lawn edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A verge is the grassy strip edging a road or path.

clue.text: Announce what's been printed from computer?

definitions.meaning: to announce aloud from a text
data output displayed or printed by a machine

explanation.surface: Declaring what came off the computer printer.
explanation.definitionFit: To read out is to announce, and a readout is information output by a computer.

clue.text: Stiffness of manner with which celebrity is given national award

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
CH is Companion of Honour, a British national award

explanation.surface: A famous person receives a national honour and becomes stuffy.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch, figuratively, means formality or stiffness of manner.

clue.text: Author abroad (penned English)

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so one piece is placed inside the other
abroad means scattered widely, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer living overseas who nevertheless wrote in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' turns AUTHOR into THORAU; 'penned' puts E inside it. The whole clue also hints at the writer, who wrote in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau was an American author, best known for Walden.

clue.text: Aim at Oxford? To finish eventually

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
up means in residence at a university such as Oxford

explanation.surface: Aiming for Oxford University and getting there in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up is to finish in a place or state eventually.

clue.text: Duck — this on the donkey in game?

definitions.meaning: a dabbling duck with a long pointed tail

definitions.text: this on the donkey in game?
definitions.meaning: the party game in which blindfolded children pin a tail on a donkey picture

explanation.surface: A duck playing a children's party game.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, pin tail is what players do in the donkey party game; as one, a duck species.

clue.text: Canon with a shape like Friar Tuck?

definitions.meaning: a canon, a song where voices enter in turn with the same tune

definitions.text: with a shape like Friar Tuck?
definitions.meaning: Robin Hood's Friar Tuck is traditionally portly and rotund

explanation.surface: A clergyman built like Robin Hood's jolly friar.
explanation.definitionFit: A round is a musical canon, and round also describes a plump figure.

clue.text: Outwardly bad-tempered, I am performing as witness

indicators.note: outwardly means one word forms the outside, wrapping the other

parts.note: testy means irritable or bad-tempered
I'm is the contraction of I am
on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: A grumpy person agrees to appear as a witness in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony is evidence given, as in bearing witness to something.

clue.text: Where potential listeners may get cornered

definitions.text: Where potential listeners may get cornered

parts.words: Where potential listeners may get cornered
parts.note: a London park famed for Speakers' Corner, where crowds gather to hear soapbox orators

explanation.surface: Audiences trapped by speakers in a well-known spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Speakers' Corner, in a large London park, is where anyone may address passers-by, so listeners are 'cornered'.
explanation.definitionFit: This London royal park contains Speakers' Corner, the traditional open-air public speaking spot.

clue.text: Church officer functioning after cross is put in place

indicators.note: after places the word for functioning at the end
is put in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to set is to put in place
X is the shape of a cross
on means working or functioning

explanation.surface: A church officer gets to work once a cross is installed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer who maintains the building and graveyard.
